title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
summary: Find the median of two sorted arrays without merging them.
statement:
Two arrays `a` and `b` are each sorted ascending. Return the median of the two combined.

With an even total length the median is the mean of the two middle values, so the answer can be a half-integer — the return type is a float and the grader compares with a tolerance.

At least one of the arrays is non-empty.

### Constraints

- 0 ≤ a.length, b.length ≤ 100,000
- 1 ≤ a.length + b.length
- -10⁹ ≤ values ≤ 10⁹
- **Required: O(log(n + m)) time.** Merging and sorting is O((n + m) log(n + m)) and does not meet the bound.

### Example

```
a = [1, 3], b = [2]      -> 2.0
a = [1, 2], b = [3, 4]   -> 2.5
```

## The idea

Do not build the merged array. Instead, cut both arrays into a left part and a right part so that:

- the two left parts together hold exactly half the elements, and
- every value on the left is `<=` every value on the right.

Once such a cut exists, the median is read straight off the four values touching it — no merging needed.

Choosing `i`, the cut in `a`, forces `j = (n + m + 1) / 2 - i`, the cut in `b`. So there is only one number to search for, and `i` can be found by binary search on the shorter array. That is where the `log` comes from: **binary search over a cut position, not over values**.

The cut is correct when `a[i-1] <= b[j]` and `b[j-1] <= a[i]`. If `a[i-1] > b[j]` the cut in `a` is too far right; otherwise it is too far left.

### Details that decide correctness

- **Search the shorter array.** If `a` is longer, swap them first, or `j` can fall outside `b`.
- **Treat the ends as infinities.** With `i = 0` there is no `a[i-1]`, so use `-∞`; with `i = n` use `+∞` for `a[i]`. This is what makes an empty array and a fully one-sided cut work without special cases.
- **Odd total:** the answer is `max(a[i-1], b[j-1])` — the largest value on the left. **Even total:** average that with `min(a[i], b[j])`.
- Use `(n + m + 1) / 2` for the half, so the odd case leaves the extra element on the left and both cases share one formula.

> **Duplicates are the usual bug**
>
> With many equal values the two conditions can both hold at several cut positions, and any of them is correct. An implementation that uses `<` where it needs `<=` will loop past the valid cut and fall out of the search.

visibleTests.explanation: Odd total, so the middle value itself.
Even total: the mean of 2 and 3.
